subtheme: A Family Television with Rabbit Ears
description: Adjust an older television's knobs and indoor antenna.
cardDescription: Adjust an older television's knobs and indoor antenna.
focus: The setting is a Family Television with Rabbit Ears. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Household set for watching broadcast shows
Rounded door handle turned by hand
Image made with a camera or pencil
Put something in a particular position
Long upholstered seat for more than one person
Small timepiece worn on the wrist
Another word for a radio antenna

answerNotes.TELEVISION: Early television sets often had tuning knobs and antennas. The particular design varied, so the scene is one example of home viewing.
answerNotes.ANTENNA: A broadcast antenna receives radio waves. Rabbit ears is a familiar nickname for a pair of adjustable indoor television rods.
answerNotes.SCREEN: Screen can mean a display surface or a mesh barrier. The phone and movie scenes use the display meaning; a porch door uses the mesh meaning.
answerNotes.DIAL: A dial can show numbers on a clock, telephone, or radio. Its marks identify times, phone choices, or station frequencies according to the object.
answerNotes.CHANNEL: A television channel identifies a broadcast choice. Turning the volume changes loudness rather than choosing a different channel.
answerNotes.KNOB: A knob is a rounded control or handle. On an older television it may turn a setting; on a door it may operate a latch.
answerNotes.WATCH: Watch can be a wrist timepiece or the action of looking attentively. A football-viewing scene uses the action rather than the object.

answerNotes.LABEL: A label identifies an item or its contents. It can carry a name, date, size, or address depending on the scene.
answerNotes.NEEDLE: A sewing needle has a point and an eye. Knitting needles generally use pointed ends to form loops without threading an eye.
answerNotes.SONG: A song has words and a melody. In the familiar-title puzzles, ordinary definitions help even when a reader does not remember the recording.
answerNotes.SPIN: Spin means rotate around a center. A top stays upright while turning quickly, then wobbles as it slows.
answerNotes.MUSIC: Music can be played by instruments or sung. A concert is an event at which music is performed, rather than the music itself.

answerNotes.RADIO: A radio receives broadcasts. Choosing a station selects a particular transmission rather than changing the recorded song itself.
answerNotes.SONG: A song has words and a melody. In the familiar-title puzzles, ordinary definitions help even when a reader does not remember the recording.
answerNotes.DIAL: A dial can show numbers on a clock, telephone, or radio. Its marks identify times, phone choices, or station frequencies according to the object.
answerNotes.VOICE: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings. A speaker is the device that reproduces the sound on a call or recording.
answerNotes.LETTER: Letter can mean a written message or one alphabet character. An envelope clue points to the message sense.
answerNotes.SPEAKER: A speaker can be a person talking or an audio device. In a video call's controls, it is the device that makes sound audible.
answerNotes.MUSIC: Music can be played by instruments or sung. A concert is an event at which music is performed, rather than the music itself.

answerNotes.REEL: A reel stores a long flexible strip or line. A fishing reel takes up line, while a film reel holds a strip of images.
answerNotes.FILM: Film can mean the strip used to record pictures or the finished movie. A projector moves the strip to display successive images.
answerNotes.CAMERA: A camera records pictures. Its lens focuses the scene, while a shutter or electronic control determines when light is recorded.
answerNotes.SCREEN: Screen can mean a display surface or a mesh barrier. The phone and movie scenes use the display meaning; a porch door uses the mesh meaning.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.LIGHT: Light makes things visible. A lamp produces light, while a mirror mainly reflects light arriving from elsewhere.
answerNotes.FRAME: A frame surrounds and supports an image or object. The glass, backing, and outer border are separate parts of a picture frame.
